name: Lying Floor Cable Hamstring Curl
description: A hamstring curl performed lying prone on the floor with a cable ankle attachment from a low pulley. Unlike the lying leg curl machine, this variation uses a cable that provides constant tension through the full range, including the lockout position where the machine lever arm would have minimal mechanical advantage. The floor position and cable angle together create a unique hamstring isolation stimulus that complements machine and dumbbell curl variations.

execution.starting_position: Lie prone on the floor facing away from a low cable pulley. Attach an ankle cuff to one ankle and connect it to the cable. Legs are extended with a slight bend in the working knee.
execution.setup_instructions: Lie far enough from the pulley that the cable is taut at full knee extension. The hip must remain flat against the floor throughout.
steps: Step 1: Begin prone with the ankle cuff attached and the leg extended.
Step 2: Curl the working leg by bending the knee, bringing the heel toward the glute.
Step 3: Hold the fully curled position for 1-2 seconds.
Step 4: Lower the leg slowly back to the extended starting position. Repeat, then switch legs.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale during the curl. Inhale during the return.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hip off the floor during the curl — the hip must stay flat
Using a cable tension so high that full range of motion is compromised
Rushing the eccentric — the slow return is where most of the hypertrophy stimulus occurs
safety_considerations: Ensure the ankle cuff is securely attached before starting
If lower back discomfort occurs, place a folded towel under the abdomen to reduce lumbar stress
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom. Maximum knee flexion (heel to glute) at the top.
coaching_cues: Keep the hip flat — do not let it rise during the curl
Feel the hamstring pull the heel toward the glute — not the glute squeezing the heel up
Slow on the way down — the cable fights you all the way back to the start
